\label{lemma-iso-on-RSheafHom}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes.
Let $a$ be the right adjoint to
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
Let $L \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and $K \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
Then the map (\ref{equation-sheafy-trace})
$$
Rf_*R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(L, a(K))
\longrightarrow
R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_Y}(Rf_*L, K)
$$
becomes an isomorphism after applying the functor
$DQ_Y : D(\mathcal{O}_Y) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
discussed in Derived Categories of Schemes, Section
\ref{perfect-section-better-coherator}.

statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Consider a cartesian square of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{matrix}
\]
where $f$ and $g$ are *Tor-independent*, meaning the higher Tor sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal O_{Y'}$ over $\mathcal O_Y$ vanish. Write $a=a_f$ and $a'=a_{f'}$ for the respective right adjoints of derived pushforward. The usual derived base-change map is $\beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*L(g')^*$; under Tor-independence it is an isomorphism. Its adjoint mate is the isomorphism $\xi:Rg'_*a'\xrightarrow{\sim} a Rg_*$. The duality base-change map is the natural transformation $\alpha:L(g')^*a\to a' Lg^*$ obtained by composing unit $\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^*$, $\xi^{-1}$, and counit $L(g')^*Rg'_*\to\mathrm{id}$. Then the canonical adjoint-mate transformation $\xi:Rg'_*a'\to a\,Rg_*$, considered as a natural transformation from $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y'})$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, is an isomorphism. This holds if $g$ is flat, and more generally whenever $f$ and $g$ are Tor-independent; the square need not be proper.

\label{lemma-when-sheafy}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes. Let $a$ be the right adjoint to
$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
Let $V \subset Y$ be quasi-compact open with inverse image $U \subset X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $Q \in D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
supported on $Y \setminus V$ the image $a(Q)$ is supported on
$X \setminus U$ if and only if (\ref{equation-sheafy})
is an isomorphism on all $K$ in $D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
\item For every $Q \in D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$
supported on $Y \setminus V$ the image $a(Q)$ is supported on
$X \setminus U$ if and only if (\ref{equation-sheafy})
is an isomorphism on all $K$ in $D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
\item If $a$ commutes with direct sums, then the equivalent conditions of
(1) imply the equivalent conditions of (2).
\end{enumerate}
statement: Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. In the cartesian open square $U=X\times_YV\xrightarrow{j'}X$, $V\xrightarrow{j}Y$ with $V\subseteq Y$ quasi-compact open, write $f_V:U\to V$ and $a_V$ for the right adjoint of $R(f_V)_*$. The *restriction comparison* is $\rho_K:(j')^*a_f(K)\to a_V(j^*K)$, obtained from the open-immersion case of the duality base-change transformation. A complex is *supported on* a closed subset if all its cohomology sheaves vanish outside that subset. Set $T=Y\setminus V$. Then: (1) $\rho_K$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ if and only if for every $Q\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ supported on $T$, the object $a_f(Q)$ is supported on $X\setminus U$. (2) The same equivalence holds without the plus/bounded-below restrictions: $\rho_K$ is an isomorphism for all $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ iff $a_f$ takes every object supported on $T$ to one supported on $X\setminus U$. (3) If $a_f$ preserves arbitrary direct sums, then the equivalent conditions in (1) imply the equivalent conditions in (2).

\label{lemma-proper-noetherian}
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism. If\footnote{This proof works for those
morphisms of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes such that
$Rf_*P$ is pseudo-coherent for all $P$ perfect on $X$. It follows
easily from a theorem of Kiehl \cite{Kiehl} that this holds if
$f$ is proper and pseudo-coherent. This is the correct generality
for this lemma and some of the other results in this chapter.}

\item $f$ is flat and of finite presentation, or
\item $Y$ is Noetherian
\end{enumerate}
then the equivalent conditions of Lemma \ref{lemma-when-sheafy} part (1)
hold for all quasi-compact opens $V$ of $Y$.

\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} a(\mathcal{O}_Y) \ar[r] &

c(K)
}

is commutative where the arrows are (\ref{equation-compare-with-pullback})
and we have used $Lh^* = Lf^* \circ Lg^*$ and $c = a \circ b$.

Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.

$\mathcal{L} = \wedge^{n + 1}(\mathcal{E})$.

$Rf_* : D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_X) \to D_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ of

$$
c : f^*\mathcal{L}(-n - 1)[n] \longrightarrow a(\mathcal{O}_Y)
$$

$X = \mathbf{P}^n_Y$ and we obtain
$a(\mathcal{O}_Y) = \mathcal{O}_X(-n - 1)[n]$.

\label{lemma-perfect-comparison-shriek}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
$\textit{FTS}_S$. Assume $f$ is perfect (e.g., flat). Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ is in $D_{\textit{Coh}}^b(\mathcal{O}_X)$,
\item[(b)] $f^!\mathcal{O}_Y$ has finite tor dimension in
$D(f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_Y)$,
\item[(c)] $\mathcal{O}_X \to
R\SheafHom_{\mathcal{O}_X}(f^!\mathcal{O}_Y, f^!\mathcal{O}_Y)$
is an isomorphism,
\item[(d)] $f^!$ maps $D_{\textit{Coh}}^b(\mathcal{O}_Y)$ into
$D_{\textit{Coh}}^b(\mathcal{O}_X)$,
\item[(e)] the map
$\mu_{f,  K} :
Lf^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} f^!\mathcal{O}_Y
\to
f^!K$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-map-pullback-to-shriek-well-defined}
is an isomorphism for all $K \in D_\QCoh^+(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
\end{enumerate}

statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Suppose $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ is a *local complete intersection morphism*: locally on its source it factors as a regular (Koszul-regular) closed immersion into a smooth $Y$-scheme. Then (1) $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is *derived-invertible*: locally on $X$ it is a shift of an invertible sheaf and admits a two-sided inverse for derived tensor product; and (2) the upper-shriek functor $f^!$ takes perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ to perfect objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, interpreted on the bounded-below subcategory where $f^!$ is defined.
